Read `ledger.beancount` in one complete call before editing it — it returns the complete ledger exactly as the scorer sees it; line endings are normalized to LF. Preserve every existing transaction. Use sliced reads or grep only for the other files when you need them.

ledger.beancount is sent to you ONCE per revision: a second complete read of a revision you have already been given returns a short receipt instead of the file, so keep the content of your last complete read. A successful write_ledger makes a new revision, and the next complete read returns it.

When you have worked out what is wrong, write the corrected ledger back with write_ledger. Post what is genuinely missing; do not remove or rewrite entries that are already there, and do not invent accounts that are not in the chart.

You may call run_beancount at any time to check that the ledger still loads.

You have 25 turns. The episode has a total ceiling of 40,000 completion tokens, including hidden reasoning. You will not receive an exact remaining-token counter, so keep responses concise and use tools early. Tool calls emitted on the turn that exhausts this token ceiling are executed; calls emitted on turn 25 are not. Call submit by turn 24 to finish early. If the episode limit is reached first, the latest successfully written ledger is scored.

The episode also ends after 3 consecutive turns without a tool call — including an unbroken run of turns cut off at the completion cap. If a reply is cut off, make the next one shorter and call a tool.

When you are finished, call submit to end the episode: the ledger as last written is final. submit needs a ledger that was written and loaded — with nothing written, or with the last write refused, it is refused too and the episode carries on.

The November checking account statement has arrived and the month needs to be closed. Bring the ledger into agreement with the statement, following the bookkeeping policy. Write the corrected ledger back to ledger.beancount.

1  # Alpine Trading Co. — Bookkeeping Policy
    2  
    3  ## Bank service charges
    4  Fees levied directly by the bank (monthly service charges, wire fees, returned
    5  item fees) are recorded to `Expenses:BankFees` on the date the bank applies them.
    6  
    7  ## Customer receipts
    8  Cash received from a customer reduces `Assets:AR`. Where the deposit reference
    9  identifies a sales invoice, it is applied against that invoice.
   10  
   11  ## Payments to suppliers
   12  The `default_account` a supplier carries in the vendor master is where that
   13  supplier's purchases are booked when they arrive. It is not where a payment to
   14  that supplier lands. Where a supplier's purchases are booked to an asset
   15  account, the goods were taken into that account when they were received and a
   16  payable was raised for them at the same time, so cash paid to that supplier
   17  afterwards settles the payable and is recorded to `Liabilities:AP`. Where a
   18  supplier's purchases are booked to an expense account, no payable is raised:
   19  the payment is the expense, and it is recorded to that supplier's own
   20  `default_account` on the day it is paid, except where it is paid ahead of the
   21  period it covers, which the prepayments section below governs.
   22  
   23  ## Outstanding checks
   24  A check that has been issued and recorded in the ledger but has not cleared the
   25  bank as at the statement cut-off date remains recorded. It is a timing
   26  difference and is listed as an outstanding item in the reconciliation. It is
   27  never removed or adjusted.
   28  
   29  ## Deposits in transit
   30  Cash recorded as received in the ledger that does not appear on the bank
   31  statement until after the cut-off date is likewise a timing difference and is
   32  listed as an outstanding item.
   33  
   34  ## Dates
   35  An entry carries the date of the transaction — the day a check was issued, a
   36  receipt was received or an invoice was raised — never the date the bank
   37  processed it. A ledger date that differs from the statement's date for the
   38  same item is not an error and is not to be changed.
   39  
   40  The bank processes a transaction on or after the day it happens, so for a
   41  customer or vendor movement the ledger date is never later than the
   42  statement's date for the same item.
   43  
   44  An item the books do not carry at all has no transaction date to keep. The
   45  statement's date is then the only date in evidence, so an entry added for a
   46  statement row the ledger is missing is posted on the date the bank shows.
   47  
   48  ## Matching the statement to the ledger
   49  A statement row and a ledger entry of the same amount and the same
   50  counterparty, dated within the clearing window for the rail the row names,
   51  are the same transaction and are treated as one item — not as two that
   52  happen to agree.
   53  
   54  ## Prepayments
   55  Amounts paid before the period they relate to are recorded to
   56  `Assets:Prepayments` and released to expense in the period they cover. Rent
   57  paid in one month for the following month is a prepayment, not an expense of
   58  the month it was paid.
   59  
   60  ## Sales tax
   61  Alpine collects sales tax from customers on sales and owes it to the state.
   62  Purchases of goods for resale are exempt, so no tax is recoverable on the
   63  purchase side.
   64  
   65  ## Suspense accounts
   66  Alpine does not operate a suspense or plug account. Every posting is made to the
   67  account that reflects the underlying transaction.

tool_defs.name: submit
tool_defs.description:
End the episode. The ledger as last written is final.

Call this once you have written a ledger with write_ledger and it loaded.
Nothing is read or changed afterwards; the ledger on disk at this moment
is what is delivered, and its content hash is fixed here.

If nothing has been stored, or if the last write_ledger was refused by the
ledger protocol, submit is refused and the episode carries on.
